subject: Mechanical Engineering
title: The Sewing Machine: Cams, Cranks, and Needles
description: A tiny lesson with a big payoff: The Sewing Machine: Cams, Cranks, and Needles.

hook.text: A sewing machine stitches 1,500 times per minute. The needle, bobbin, and feed all move in perfect sync.

buildup.text: A crank converts the motor's rotation into the needle's up-and-down motion. A cam controls the fabric feed.

discovery.text: The lockstitch was the key. Two threads interlock inside the fabric, creating a stitch that won't unravel.

twist.text: Isaac Singer didn't invent it. Elias Howe did. Singer improved the design and built a marketing empire.

climax.text: The sewing machine combines cranks, cams, gears, levers, and springs in one compact, precise package.

punchline.text: Six mechanisms working in sync, 1,500 times a minute. That's engineering.

quiz.question: What mechanism moves the needle in a sewing machine?
options: A solenoid that pulls the needle with electromagnetic force
A crank that converts motor rotation into up-and-down motion
Pneumatic pressure that alternately pushes and pulls the needle
